title: Forward+: Horizontal NaN lines appear in specular reflections on fully smooth materials when Light3D Size is above `0.0`
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: 4.5.beta1, 4.5.stable, 4.6.dev2 - Not reproducible in: 4.4.stable, 4.5.dev5 ### System information Godot v4.6.dev (c7b176756) - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7688) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 63.55 GiB memory ### Issue description Horizontal NaN lines appear in specular reflections on fully smooth materials (`roughness = 0.0`) when Light3D's **Size** (**Angular Distance** for DirectionalLight3D) is above `0.0`: (There are NaNs - if you enable SSIL, the whole scene turns black as a result.) The lines' appearance change according to the mesh subdivision level (a subdivided plane will have shorter lines). All light types are affected. Unlike https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/110207, this issue is reproducible in Forward+ but **not** in Mobile due to the specular lobe size not being affected by the Light3D **Size** property in Mobile. Compatibility looks correct. The issue is reproducible both in Vulkan and Direct3D 12. When using Direct3D 12, it's also reproducible with WARP software rendering (`--gpu-index 1`), although the appearance of the lines will be slightly different: The red light on the left has its Size set to `0.0`, while the green light has Size set to `0.5` and the blue light uses `1.0`. This reflection's strength is also not affected by the Light3D Specular property. It completely disappears if Specular is exactly `0.0`, but will appear identical regardless of its value otherwise: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/034c7afd-1fd4-4209-928b-3411c2e9656c ### Steps to reproduce - Add an OmniLight3D, SpotLight3D or DirectionalLight3D at a grazing angle above a floor with `roughness = 0.0`. - Increase the Light3D's Size or Angular Distance property. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [specular-lobe.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23031949/specular-lobe.zip)
